_comment: Branches of the modelled oref0 files that no input reaches, with the argument. Key: file:line:kind:outcome, as in docs/COVERAGE.md. `quote` lists source lines (file, from, to) that scripts/coverage/report.js copies from vendor/oref0/lib into docs/COVERAGE.md. `scope` says under which calls the argument holds.

glucose-get-last.js:11:if:1.why: The filter keeps only readings with `obj.glucose || obj.sgv` truthy, and the map then sets `obj.glucose` to that truthy value, so `obj.glucose !== null` always holds.

glucose-get-last.js:37:if:1.why: `getDateFromEntry` returns `entry.date` if it is truthy and otherwise the value of `Date.parse(...)`, which is always a number (possibly NaN); `now_date` is that value or, after line 49, a sum of two such values divided by 2. Neither is ever `undefined`, so the `typeof ... !== 'undefined'` test always holds.

determine-basal/determine-basal.js:1011:.why: `minDelta` is assigned once, `Math.min(glucose_status.delta, glucose_status.short_avgdelta)`, so `delta < minDelta` is false whenever both are numbers. If either is NaN, `minDelta` is NaN and the enclosing test `minDelta < expectedDelta` (line 1008) is false. `glucose_status.delta` is a number because `glucose_status` comes from `getLastGlucose` (as in bin/oref0-determine-basal.js and both difftests), which returns `Math.round(last_delta * 100) / 100`.
determine-basal/determine-basal.js:1011:.scope: determine_basal called with the output of getLastGlucose

iob/index.js:10:if:1.why: `generate`'s third argument is passed only by determine-basal/cob.js line 147 and determine-basal/autosens.js line 181 (COB and autosens, which LeanAID does not model; see QUIRK Q10). oref0's loop (bin/oref0-calculate-iob.js) calls `generate(inputs)`, and `LeanAID.Iob.generate` transcribes that call: it always finds the treatments in the history.

iob/calculate.js:17:if:0.why: `iobCalc` is called only by total.js line 72, with `time`, the argument of `iobTotal` on which line 5 already called `time.getTime()` (it would have thrown if `time` were undefined).

iob/total.js:18:if:0.why: `opts.treatments` is set by index.js lines 10-16 and 20-32: the result of `find_insulin`, which always returns an array (history.js lines 568-570), or the caller's `treatments`, which is truthy on that path, or `[]`. Arrays are truthy.

iob/history.js:12:if:1.why: `splitTimespanWithOneSplitter` is called only by `splitTimespan`, with the elements of its `splitterMoments` argument, and `splitTimespan` is called only with `splitterEvents`, every element of which is built with `type = 'recurring'`.

iob/history.js:105:if:0.scope: pump histories whose timestamps are ISO-8601 date-times
iob/history.js:105:if:0.why: Taking these branches needs `currentlySuspended` and a numeric comparison with `lastSuspendTime`, which is the suspend's timestamp *string* (line 234), QUIRK Q7. JavaScript converts it with Number(), which is NaN for an ISO-8601 date-time such as `2026-11-18T07:00:00-05:00` or `2026-11-18T12:00:00.000Z`, so line 105 is false. A string that Number() converts, such as epoch milliseconds, makes it true, but moment cannot parse such a string, so `new Date(lastSuspendTime)` is an Invalid Date and line 482, which runs in the same call (these lines run only with `suspend_zeros_iob`, line 424, and line 479 tests the same `currentlySuspended`), throws RangeError: oref0 returns no IOB to compare (tried: scripts/difftest/make-iob-targeted.js). Only a timestamp that both Number() and Date accept, such as a bare year `"2026"`, avoids the throw; pump histories do not have such timestamps. Line 105's second operand (outcome 1 of the binary-expr) is reached.
